## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kusalattika* ("Triad on the Wholesome") is the primary triad division of the *Tikapaṭṭhāna*, forming the second section of the *Paṭṭhāna* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. It serves as the foundational model for the text's exhaustive inquiry into conditional relations (*paccaya*), examining how phenomena classified as wholesome (*kusala*), unwholesome (*akusala*), or indeterminate/neutral (*abyākata*) condition one another [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Its exposition is methodically organized into structural chapters such as the "dependent chapter" (*paṭicca-vāra*), systematically tracing relations under the twenty-four conditions—including root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*) and object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*)—in both positive and negative analytical modes [Nyanatiloka 2007]. In commentarial and sectarian debates, such as discussions concerning the Abhayagiri tradition's view that ascetic practices (*dhutaṅga*) are mere designations (*paññatti*), the *Kusalattika* commentary (*kusalattikavaṇṇanā*) serves as an authoritative benchmark for whether phenomena fall within or outside ultimate classifications [Chandawimala, Impact of the Abhayagiri Practices].

**Sources**

- [Chandawimala, Impact of the Abhayagiri Practices] Rangama Chandawimala Thero, Impact of the Abhayagiri Practices on Development of Theravada Buddhism in Sri Lanka — Citation of commentarial exegesis on the Kusalattika concerning Abhayagiri views on dhutaṅgas.
